chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Gi Earth is the garden, and you nurture whatever is in front of you. In a situationship you probably give a lot: you listen, you help, you remember things, you make every evening cozy. You stay because caring is your way of loving, and because part of you hopes that enough care will eventually turn this into something real. Ask yourself, gently but honestly: is this growing because of us, or only because of me? If you stopped watering it for two weeks, would anything still be standing? That question can sting a little. Answer it anyway, quietly, just for yourself.
text.what-you-want: You want to be taken care of too. Gi Earth often forgets to put that on the list at all. Think practically for a moment: what would care from them actually look like? Checking in on a hard day, making the plan for once, showing up when you're stressed without being asked. You're allowed to want a partner who tends your garden as well as their own. It's not asking too much. It's asking for even, which is the minimum for anything you'd call a relationship. Write down three small acts of care you'd love to receive. Specifics make it easier to notice when they're missing.
text.mixed-signals: Faced with mixed signals, you worry, and then you try harder. More effort, more help, more thoughtful little gestures. Gi Earth hopes that care will create clarity. Usually it creates comfort for the other person instead, and comfortable people rarely feel any urgency to define things. Pause your effort for a short while and simply see what they do on their own. Their unprompted effort, the plans they make and the check-ins they start, is a far more honest signal than how warmly they respond to yours. Two weeks is usually enough to see the real shape of things without your hands holding it up.
text.the-talk: The talk, for you, should be practical and kind. Gi Earth is good at sensible, grounded conversations. Try: I've really enjoyed this, and I need to know if we're moving toward something real. Resist the strong urge to soften it with but no worries if not. There are worries, and that's fine. Your needs aren't a bother or an imposition. Let them be real in the room. Then give them space to answer honestly, even if the honest answer isn't the one you were hoping for. Make it a calm daytime conversation, not a late-night one where you're tired and more likely to back down.
text.your-line: Where you draw the line: one-sided effort. Decide what minimum mutual care looks like for you, written down in plain terms. If you keep doing all the planning, all the checking in, all the emotional work while they simply turn up, that's your line crossed. Stepping back doesn't mean abandoning them or being unkind. It means leaving a garden that never fed you, so you have the energy to plant one that will. You can be gentle and still be finished. Notice how you feel on Sunday evenings. If it's drained rather than full, your body already knows where the line is.
text.either-way: Whichever way it goes, your care isn't wasted. It's who you are, and it goes with you. If they want more, make sure it's balanced from the very first week. If not, redirect all that warmth toward yourself and toward the people who already return it. Gi Earth heals well with routine, good food, and friends who notice you. You'll grow something new, and this time it will be properly tended from both sides, which is what you deserved all along. Start with something small and selfish this week: a meal you love, an evening that belongs to nobody else.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You make everything so warm for them, Gi.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Unpaid caretaking for someone who won't commit. Love that for you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're allowed to want care back.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And stop saying 'no worries if not'. There are worries.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Pause the effort and see what they do.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Their effort without prompting. That's the only data that counts.

spring.intro: Spring soil feeds whatever's planted in it. Your birth season belonged to Wood, Gi, and Wood controls Earth, so you instinctively make space for other people to grow. In a situationship you've probably been nourishing them generously: listening to their stress, backing their plans, being the soft landing. They grow. You wait. Spring Gi tends to think that if you tend well enough, commitment will sprout on its own. Sometimes the seed just isn't the kind that roots. Look at what you get back. Are they tending you at all? Good soil deserves a gardener too, not just a tenant.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're their emotional support garden. Unpaid. No lease. Think about that, Gi.

summer.intro: Summer Gi is warm, fertile and full of care. Your season belonged to Fire and Fire feeds Earth, so you're well supported inside and generous on the outside. In a situationship you probably create comfort without trying: the cozy nights in, the little care packages, the way you remember things. The risk for warm Gi is building a relationship's whole atmosphere without its commitment. They get the home feeling without the home. Summer Gi's question is simple. If you stopped hosting, what would they bring to the table? You're not asking too much by wanting a guest who becomes a partner.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You make everything cozy. You deserve someone who brings the blanket too.

autumn.intro: Autumn is harvest, and Gi Earth is the thing being harvested. Your birth season belonged to Metal and Earth gives rise to Metal, so you pour yourself into results: helpful, competent, always delivering. In a situationship you might be over-performing to stay valuable. Never needy, always easy, always useful. Autumn Gi's blind spot is believing affection has to be earned with output. It doesn't. Notice how much of this connection depends on you giving and them receiving. Try being slightly less useful for two weeks. What remains when you stop producing is what's really between you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Try being less helpful for two weeks. Terrifying, I know. Do it anyway.

winter.intro: Winter Gi is soil holding cold water: absorbent, quiet, carrying more than it shows. Water was in command when you were born, and Earth controls Water, so you're always shaping feelings into something manageable. In a situationship you probably absorb the ambiguity for both of you. Their mixed signals soak into you and you turn them into reasons to stay. Winter Gi can go muddy: everything blurred, no clear edges. What you need is a firm line, even a small one. Decide what would make you feel secure, say a weekly plan or a real label, and say it plainly. Clear edges make soil fertile, not soggy.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A small, clear line is kind to both of you, Gi.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Gi, your own element runs strong. You're the garden: you notice what someone needs and quietly provide it. In a situationship that turns into doing relationship things without a relationship: the snacks, the check-ins, the remembering. They get the benefits of partnership, and you get the uncertainty. The drift is you tending something they haven't committed to tend back. The talk for you is about fairness, said kindly. What are we building, and are we both building it?

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You've been tending this garden alone, Gi. Ask who else holds a shovel.

strength.strong: Your soil is rich and well fed, Gi, which makes you confident in how you care. A strong Gi tends to steer: planning their weekends, advising their decisions, organizing the whole connection. It comes from love. It can also make them feel managed instead of chosen. The blind spot is caring so capably that they never have to show up. Leave a little space empty and see whether they fill it. What they bring unprompted is the real signal, far more than anything you arrange.
strength.weak: With little support in your chart, Gi, you give from soil that's already stretched. In a situationship you're probably the emotional caretaker: their stress, their schedule, their feelings first. You make yourself low effort so you're never a burden. The blind spot is that caretaking can hide the fact that nobody is taking care of you. Ask for one thing this week: a call, a plan, a reply. How they respond to a small need tells you a lot about how they'd handle bigger ones.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practice clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyze every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analyzed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: Comfortable enough to skip the label
gap-wood.text: With a Gap Wood, you feel useful, safe and a little bit in love, maybe in that order. Gap has plans and you have a talent for making plans actually work. You remember their dentist appointment. You know which coffee they like. You've helped them rewrite a cover letter at 11 p.m. on a Tuesday. What you haven't done is ask what this is, because asking feels like making a fuss. The drift in this pair is the soil quietly adapting. Gap is direct and assumes that if there were a problem, you'd say so. You assume that if they cared, they'd notice. So the question sits in your chest while you keep watering. Your signal is devotion, and it can read as being fine with anything. The talk feels overdue only in your head, so be kind to yourself about it. Gap responds well to plain words, so try: I really like you, and I'd like to be your partner, not just your helper. Is that what you want too? It's not a fuss. It's a fair question from someone who has earned the right to ask it, and Gap Wood tends to respect people who ask.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 甲己 is a lovely pull. Comfort is not the same as clarity, though.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gi, you know their coffee order. You should know where you stand.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap needs to ask how Gi is. Really ask.

eul-wood.title: Who is feeding whom in this garden
eul-wood.text: An Eul Wood brings color into your week: memes at lunch, a voice note about a dream they had, a plan for a picnic that may or may not happen. You love it. You also notice you're the one who checks the train times, remembers their mom's birthday and asks whether the picnic is actually happening. Eul answers the fun questions and floats past the practical ones. The drift in this pair is you giving and Eul growing, until you feel a little tired and can't quite say why. You worry about where this is going, and Eul tends to wave worries away as overthinking. So you stop mentioning them. You keep helping. And somewhere in there, the question of what you are gets composted with everything else you didn't say. Your signal is care. Eul may read it as the natural weather of you, not as a question. For the talk, you're allowed to ask for something. It's not a burden. Try: I really like you, and I've been giving a lot to this. I'd like us to be official, and I'd like it to feel more equal. Where do you stand? Say it before you're exhausted, not after.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you're allowed to have needs in this garden too.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul should answer the practical question before the meme. Every time.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Equal is a fair thing to ask for.

byeong-fire.title: Sunshine and the forgotten errand
byeong-fire.text: A Byeong Fire is sunshine on your garden. They take you out of your head, drag you to the rooftop party, make you laugh until your stomach hurts. With Byeong, you feel lighter. You also feel like the one keeping track of everything. Who's booking, what time, whether Byeong actually remembered your sister's birthday dinner. Byeong sends sunny, rapid, half-finished messages. You send caring questions, and some of them never get answered. The drift in this pair is a small one that grows. Byeong forgets details; you notice. You worry about where this is going; Byeong might wave it off as overthinking. So you keep quiet, keep helping, and keep the worry inside, and the soil slowly dries. Your signal is care, and a sun can read care as just how you are, not as you asking for something. For the talk, try not to audit. Enjoy the sunshine and still ask clearly: I love how you make me feel. I'd like us to be official, and I'd like you to show up for the small things too. Is that something you want? Name one specific small thing. Byeong does better with one clear request than with ten worries.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sun on the garden. Things genuinely grow here.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong should answer Gi's questions. Yes, the boring ones.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, enjoy the sunshine without auditing it.

jeong-fire.title: 'Are we okay?' answered with 'did you eat?'
jeong-fire.text: A Jeong Fire makes your careful world glow. They tell you how they feel, which you find both lovely and slightly alarming, because you show feelings by doing things. You've made them soup. You've checked their train times. You've texted 'did you eat?' more times than you can count. The drift in this pair is a translation problem. Jeong asks 'are we okay?' and you reply 'did you sleep?'. You both meant love. Jeong may hear your question as avoiding theirs. You may hear Jeong's as one more thing to worry about. Both of you worry, in different directions, and together you can spiral late at night, each in your own lane. Neither of you likes direct conflict, so the question of what this is stays politely unspoken. Your signal is practical care, and Jeong might want it said in words as well as done in soup. For the talk, answer the feeling question first. Literally say 'yes, we're okay' when Jeong asks, then add what you want: I care about you a lot, and I'd like to make it official. How does that sound to you? Then you can ask if they ate.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Candlelight in the kitchen. So cozy it hurts.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'Are we okay?' is not answered by 'did you eat?'

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Answer their question first. Then ask yours.

mu-earth.title: The invisible work in the valley
mu-earth.text: A Mu Earth is the mountain beside your valley: steady, protective, and completely unbothered by most things. You find that calming. When you're worrying, Mu shrugs and says 'it'll be fine', and part of you relaxes and part of you wants to scream. The drift here is your quiet effort. You ask the caring questions, you plan the weekends, you remember the things Mu forgets. Mu replies briefly, solidly, and seems happy. Mu may genuinely not see how much you're carrying, because you're good at carrying it quietly. You both avoid conflict, so the question of what this is goes unasked while you keep doing all the small things. Mu tends to read silence as all being well. You assume that if Mu cared, Mu would bring it up. Your signal is devotion, which Mu tends to experience as the natural climate of you. For the talk, say what you need before you're tired of saying nothing. Plainly: I really like you, and I've been doing a lot of the work here. I'd like us to be official and share it. Can we? Trust that Mu's brevity isn't indifference. And ask Mu to ask you questions sometimes.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mountain and valley. One landscape, two moods.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu's 'don't worry' has never helped a Gi in recorded history.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, say what you need before you're tired.

gi-earth.title: The snacks are planned, the relationship isn't
gi-earth.text: Two Gi Earths in a situationship look after each other beautifully. You both text 'home safe?'. You both remember the other's allergies. You've already planned a weekend away down to the snacks, and you did it together in a shared note. It's tender and tidy. It's also slightly anxious, because neither of you has asked what this is. The drift here is politeness. You both say yes to everyone else, then arrive at each other tired. You both avoid confrontation, so small worries get composted rather than discussed. And when you both worry about the same thing, nobody is there to say 'it'll be fine'. The 'what are we' question can become a shared silent worry: each of you wondering if the other wants it, each too considerate to put them on the spot. Your texts are caring and practical, 'did you eat?', 'I bought the thing', and very little that isn't a task. For the talk, take turns being brave. One of you just says it: I'd like us to be official. Do you feel the same? Then send a message today that isn't a task. Just a 'thinking of you'. You both deserve to be on the receiving end.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two gardens sharing a fence. So careful with each other.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You've planned the snacks for a trip but not the relationship.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Send one message today that isn't a task.

gyeong-metal.title: 'Done. Coming home.' and the question nobody answered
gyeong-metal.text: A Gyeong Metal is raw ore, and you're the fertile ground that shapes it with patience. You see what's good in them under the rough edges. They feel steadier with you around. You make their life work; they protect yours. The drift in this situationship is you becoming support staff. Gyeong texts 'done. coming home.' and you reply 'great, how did it go?' and get no answer to the question. You hold back your worries because Gyeong gets impatient. When Gyeong says something harsh, you keep it inside. Over time you can start to feel like you're working for this situationship rather than being in it. And you might notice that Gyeong mostly messages when something is needed. Your signal is patience, which steel can mistake for being fine with anything. For the talk, say what you need instead of hinting. Gyeong responds to clarity: I like you a lot. I want to be your partner, not the person who keeps everything running. I'd like us to be official, and I'd like you to ask about me more. Can you do that? It's not too much to ask. It's the minimum.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Fertile ground for raw ore. Patience that shapes strength.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong should answer when Gi asks how the day went.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, partner, not support staff. Say it.

sin-metal.title: Who moved the forks
sin-metal.text: A Sin Metal is the precious thing on your workbench. You're careful with them, they appreciate how careful you are, and together you make things beautiful. You've probably had the most perfectly arranged picnic of your life with Sin. The drift in this situationship is two perfectionists being polite. Sin notices details and sometimes fixes them. You arrange the dinner table; Sin moves the forks. You spend the whole evening wondering what was wrong with your forks. Sin's critiques, however small, set off your worry, and you lose sleep over them. You can start to find Sin cold or demanding. Sin can find you fussy or anxious. Neither of you likes confrontation, so issues stay under the politeness, and so does the 'what are we' question. Your texts take ten minutes on both ends, each crafted, each reread. Your signal is care, which Sin may see as worry. For the talk, send something silly first. A badly lit photo of a duck. Then say it plainly, in fewer words than you'd like: I want to be with you. Do you want me too? And if the forks bother you, say that too. It's allowed.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The jeweler's workbench. Careful hands, precious result.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin should leave the forks where Gi put them. Please.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, send the badly lit duck. Then say it.

im-water.title: The pigeon meme and 'are we still on?'
im-water.text: An Im Water is the flood that hits your careful garden. Exciting, overwhelming, and completely unlike anyone you'd normally choose. Im takes you to places you'd never book, talks about ideas you'd never think of, and makes you laugh at your own worries. The drift in this situationship is unpredictability. Im sends twenty messages in an hour, then nothing for a day. Plans change on the morning of. You ask a practical question, are we still on for Saturday, and get a meme instead of an answer. You worry. Im dismisses the worry as overthinking. So you try to manage it: more check-ins, more plans, more questions. Im feels managed, and gets restless. Over time you can feel drained, like a garden after a flood. Your signal is planning, which a river can feel as walls. For the talk, ask for one small, clear thing rather than many: I really like you. I'd like us to be official, and I need one message from you a day, even a tiny one. Could you give me that? Then try to stop counting. And ask Im to answer your practical question before the meme. It makes a surprising difference.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The garden and the flood. Care meets chaos.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im should answer 'are we still on?' before the pigeon meme.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, one message a day is enough. Then stop counting.

gye-water.title: 'What's wrong?' 'Nothing.'
gye-water.text: A Gye Water is gentle rain on your garden: soft, intuitive and quietly beautiful. They make your careful world feel more poetic. You make their drifting world feel more grounded. When it works, it's lovely. The drift in this situationship happens in the murky middle. Gye's moods shift, and you try to organize them: a plan to cheer them up, a list of things that might help, a question about what's wrong. Gye feels managed and says 'nothing'. You both spend the evening pretending. You start tidying; Gye starts drifting. The issue never gets a name, and neither does what you are. Gye's changes make you anxious. Your attempts to fix can feel controlling to Gye. Both of you avoid conflict, so the resentments build quietly, like damp under the floorboards. Your signal is helpfulness, which a raindrop can feel as being steered. For the talk, don't come with a solution. Come with a question and leave room: I really like you. I'd love for us to be a proper couple. How do you feel about it? And when Gye says 'nothing', try saying 'okay, I'm here when you want to talk', and then actually leave it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Rain on the garden. Gentle, if nobody fights over the mud.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'What's wrong?' 'Nothing.' The longest evening in history.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, give half an answer. Gi, give some space.
